title: Inverse image preserves scalar matrices and their cokernels
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $R=\Lambda(*)$, and let $h:V\to U$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use their small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], coefficient rings $\Lambda_U,\Lambda_V$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], canonical ring isomorphism $\alpha_h:h^{-1}\Lambda_U\cong\Lambda_V$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], and module pullback $h^*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For $m,n\geq0$ and a matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(R)$, let $A_U:\Lambda_U^m\to\Lambda_U^n$ and $A_V:\Lambda_V^m\to\Lambda_V^n$ act by the images of the same entries under the canonical scalar maps [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Here finite free modules and cokernels use [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. The regular-module comparison induced by $\alpha_h$, and its finite-coproduct extensions $e_r:h^*(\Lambda_U^r)\cong\Lambda_V^r$, satisfy $e_n\circ h^*(A_U)=A_V\circ e_m$. They induce an isomorphism $h^*\operatorname{coker}(A_U)\cong\operatorname{coker}(A_V)$ compatible with the cokernel projections.

proof.text: Write $F=h^{-1}$ for inverse image on abelian sheaves, $H=h^*$ for module pullback, and $\alpha=\alpha_h$. For $a\in R$, let $t_a:\Lambda\to\Lambda$ be multiplication by the section $a$ in the condensed ring: explicitly $t_a=\mu_\Lambda\circ(a\otimes1)\circ\lambda_\Lambda^{-1}$, with $a:\mathbf1\to\Lambda$. Put $t_{a,W}:\Lambda_W\to\Lambda_W$ for multiplication by its canonical scalar image, for $W=U,V$. The transported multiplication and unit in the pulled-back coefficient ring give $p_W^*(t_a)=t_{a,W}$: substitute the displayed formula into the strong monoidal comparison. The comparison $c:Fp_U^*\cong p_V^*$ is natural in all condensed abelian sheaves, and $c_\Lambda=\alpha$. Its naturality square for $t_a$ therefore gives $\alpha\circ F(t_{a,U})=t_{a,V}\circ\alpha$. This uses the canonical scalar maps, rather than arbitrary sections of $\Lambda_U$.

source.place: The monoidal natural isomorphism; naturality at multiplication by a section, using the transported coefficient-ring structure

proof.text: The formula for transport of module actions identifies $\operatorname{mapMod}(F)(\Lambda_U)$ with the regular module over $T=F\Lambda_U$: both actions are $F(\mu_{\Lambda_U})$ preceded by the tensor comparison. Hence $H\Lambda_U=S\otimes_T T$, where $S=\Lambda_V$ has right $T$-action $b\cdot x=b\alpha(x)$. Apply the mixed-bimodule right unitor with $P=S$, left ring $S$, and right ring $T$. It gives the canonical regular-module isomorphism $e_1:S\otimes_T T\cong S$ with $e_1\circ q=\mu_S\circ(1\otimes\alpha)$ and inverse $b\mapsto q(b\otimes1_T)$. The ring-homomorphism property of $\alpha$ gives the commuting actions required here. All tensor and coequalizer hypotheses hold for abelian sheaves: their sheaf tensor product preserves colimits in both variables, and the ambient abelian category has coequalizers. The expression $q(b\otimes x)$ denotes the map from $S\otimes T$ into the balancing coequalizer, not a claim that sections of a sheafified tensor product are all simple tensors.

source.place: Last sentence, finite free modules; regular-module case supplied by the existing mixed-bimodule right-unitor node

proof.text: By the module adjunction $H\dashv h_*$ and preservation of colimits by a left adjoint, $H$ preserves the initial object, each finite coproduct, and every coequalizer. Only finite small indexing categories are needed. In the abelian module categories the initial object is zero, so $H(0)=0$ up to its unique isomorphism, and $H$ preserves zero morphisms because they factor through zero. Define $e_r:H(\Lambda_U^r)\cong\Lambda_V^r$ by the coproduct comparison and $r$ copies of $e_1$. It is characterized by $e_r H(\iota_{j,U})=\iota_{j,V}e_1$. For each $i$, one also has $\pi_{i,V}e_r=e_1H(\pi_{i,U})$: precompose with every $H(\iota_{j,U})$ and use $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and preservation of zero. Equality follows from the coproduct universal property. This includes $r=0$, where $e_0$ is the unique isomorphism of zero objects.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1), lines 3472 ff.; finite discrete diagrams and the parallel-pair diagram

proof.text: The definition of extension of scalars sends a map $f$ to the map induced by $1_S\otimes F(f)$. For $f=t_{a,U}$, precompose both $e_1H(t_{a,U})$ and $t_{a,V}e_1$ with the balancing coequalizer map $q:S\otimes T\to S\otimes_T T$. The first composite is $\mu_S\circ(1\otimes(\alpha F(t_{a,U})))$; step 1 makes it $\mu_S\circ(1\otimes(t_{a,V}\alpha))$. This equals $t_{a,V}\circ\mu_S\circ(1\otimes\alpha)$ by associativity and commutativity of multiplication in $S$. Thus the second composite agrees. Uniqueness in the coequalizer universal property gives $e_1H(t_{a,U})=t_{a,V}e_1$.

source.place: The map induced by tensoring a morphism; explicit calculation using steps 1 and 2

proof.text: For each input $j<m$ and output $i<n$, the matrix definitions say $\pi_{i,U} A_U\iota_{j,U}=t_{a_{ij},U}$ and $\pi_{i,V} A_V\iota_{j,V}=t_{a_{ij},V}$. Using the projection and injection equations of step 3 and then step 4, compute $\pi_{i,V}e_n H(A_U)H(\iota_{j,U})=e_1H(\pi_{i,U}A_U\iota_{j,U})=t_{a_{ij},V}e_1=\pi_{i,V}A_V e_mH(\iota_{j,U})$. The coproduct property of the family $H(\iota_{j,U})$ and the product property of the projections $\pi_{i,V}$ yield $e_nH(A_U)=A_Ve_m$. For $m=0$ the domain is zero by step 3; for $n=0$ the codomain is zero. Thus the empty-index cases follow by the same universal properties. This argument needs no assertion that $F$ is linear over an untransported scalar ring.

source.place: 'Constructible complexes', local coefficient models on strata: entrywise calculation, filling the omitted scalar-matrix argument

proof.text: Let $q_U:\Lambda_U^n\to Q_U$ and $q_V:\Lambda_V^n\to Q_V$ be the cokernel projections. A cokernel is the coequalizer of its map and zero. By step 3, $H(q_U)$ is therefore a cokernel of $H(A_U)$. The matrix square of step 5 gives $q_Ve_nH(A_U)=0$ and $H(q_U)e_n^{-1}A_V=0$. The two cokernel universal properties give unique maps $u:H(Q_U)\to Q_V$ and $v:Q_V\to H(Q_U)$ satisfying $uH(q_U)=q_Ve_n$ and $vq_V=H(q_U)e_n^{-1}$. Their composites satisfy $uvq_V=q_V$ and $vuH(q_U)=H(q_U)$; uniqueness of the respective cokernel factorizations yields $uv=1$ and $vu=1$. Thus $u$ is the required isomorphism, and its defining equation is precisely compatibility with the cokernel projections.
